text.portWarn: Note: {w}. Saving still works; the connection starts as soon as the port is free.
text.tipsHint: Suggestions from the answer times measured since the start; check them against the vendor's documentation.
text.tipTimeoutUp: {p} % of the requests got no answer within {t} ms, and the slowest answer came close to it. A timeout of {s} ms should be enough.
text.tipTimeoutsFast: {p} % of the requests got no answer although the slowest answer took only {m} ms: the device drops requests. Check the unit id, for RS485 the wiring and the pause between requests; some devices take only one client at a time or need a pause after connecting.
text.tipTimeoutDown: No timeouts, the slowest answer took {m} ms. With a timeout of {s} ms instead of {t} ms the clients notice an outage sooner.
text.tipCache: {n} clients ask this device. If they read the same registers, a cache of 1000 ms answers many requests without asking the device.
text.tipCacheSaves: The cache answered {p} % of the requests without asking the device.
text.tipQueue: Up to {q} requests waited at the same time (average answer {a} ms): the device can hardly keep up. Turn on the cache or let the clients poll less often.
text.tipExceptions: The device answered {p} % of the requests with an error, usually an address it does not know. Check the registers in the clients (“Per unit id” shows which unit).
text.movedOne: {d} is missing, but the adapter seems to be plugged in elsewhere (same kind, free):
text.movedMany: {d} is missing. Several free adapters of this kind are plugged in: which one is it?
text.movedAsk: Switch “{n}” to {d}? The connection then starts with this adapter.
text.mbRoutesHint: One port for several devices: a client asking this unit is answered by another Modbus connection's device, in turn with that connection's clients. A write must be allowed by both connections.
text.mbRoutesNone: One port for several devices: this needs another Modbus connection.
text.testcaseTipEo: The last telegrams as a file for an issue; sender and base IDs are replaced by made-up ones. The dev server plays them back.
text.testcaseTipMb: The last requests and answers as a file for an issue, without client addresses. The dev server plays them back as a device.
text.testcaseTipSerial: The last data as a file for an issue. Note: meter telegrams contain the meter's number. The dev server plays them back.
text.mbWriteRegistersHint: Empty: all. Otherwise addresses and ranges like 40100-40120 47000; a write outside is refused with exception 02, also for the clients that may write.
text.eoSendersText3: Every sender ID since the start: how often, last, reception (above −75 dBm good, below −88 dBm weak) and through how many repeaters. Helps to place repeaters and to find a new switch's ID: press it and copy it here.
text.eoSendersText2: Every sender ID since the start: how often, last and through how many repeaters. Helps to find a new switch's ID: press it and copy it here. ESP2 gateways do not report reception.
text.eoSendersNew: New ones only (first heard more than 5 minutes after the start)
text.maintText: Only one computer may connect for a while, e.g. for the vendor's service program or a firmware update over RFC2217. All other clients, Home Assistant too, are disconnected and refused. Afterwards, at the latest when the app restarts, everything is as before.
text.maintAsk: Disconnect all clients of “{n}” and allow only {h} for {m} minutes?
text.maintActive: Maintenance: only {h} may connect, about {m} minutes left.
text.disconnectAsk: Disconnect all clients of “{n}”? They can connect again right away; most do so by themselves.
text.restartText: Closes the device and opens it again; all clients are disconnected and connect again.
text.usbResetText: The USB reset also resets the adapter, as if it were unplugged and plugged in again (without cutting the power). A hung firmware in the device itself sometimes still needs a power cycle.
text.restartAuto: Automatically after {m} min without data: {a} (at most 3 times in a row, then only the warning).
text.powerAsk: Cut the power of “{n}” for 5 seconds with {s}? {c} client(s) are disconnected and connect again.
text.powerSub: A switch in Home Assistant that cuts the power of the device or its USB hub. Helps when a restart and a USB reset are not enough.
text.powerSwitchHint: Leave empty if there is none. Nothing else that matters may hang on this switch, least of all Home Assistant itself. With “Then” set to a restart, one power cycle follows three restarts that did not help.
text.restartAsk: Restart “{n}”? The {c} connected clients are disconnected and can connect again right away.
text.usbResetAsk: Reset the USB adapter of “{n}”? The connection restarts and the {c} connected clients are disconnected; it takes a few seconds.
text.sClientsSub: Who connects to your ports. Tap a computer to see its history, name it or block it. Changes apply at once.
text.clientAuto_app: app in the Supervisor network, connected now
text.newClientsFull: The list is full: further new computers appear once there is room here.
text.clientForgetAsk: Remove {h} from the list? Its name is lost; if it connects again it is reported as new.
text.blockAsk: Block {h}? This computer is disconnected at once and refused by every connection until you release it. On serial connections all clients are briefly disconnected.
text.blockHint: Applies to all connections. Home Assistant, the apps and this host cannot be blocked.
text.blockCustom: Not for the ports of your own ser2net.yaml: there you list the allowed addresses yourself.
text.notifyNewClients: Notify when a new computer connects
text.connectionsSub: Serial and Modbus devices and EnOcean gateways, shared over the network.
text.missingHint: {d} is not plugged in. Check the USB stick and cable.
text.emptyText: Add a connection or take over your existing ser2net or modbus-proxy configuration.
text.customActive: Your own ser2net.yaml is in use
text.customActiveText: The forms are kept but not used. ser2net's ports:
text.liveSub: Read from ser2net's trace – takes no client place.
text.liveAutoOpen: The card opens as soon as data arrives.
text.liveEmpty: No data yet. ser2net opens the device only while a client is connected – or with “keep device open”.
text.why_local: Not reachable: the connection is bound to this host (bind address or network “this host only”).
text.why_clients: Not reachable: this connection's own allowed clients ({a}) exclude this address. They override the network setting; leave them empty to follow it.
text.why_network: Not reachable: the address is outside the network setting (Settings → Network).
text.lineUnsupported: The driver does not count errors.
text.lineClosed: Counted only while the device is open.
text.tplConfirm: The template overwrites the matching fields of this connection, for example baud rate, mode and clients. Continue?
text.templateSub: Fills in the fields; everything stays editable.
text.mbProfileSub: Starting values for this vendor's devices; everything stays editable. The client sets the unit. When in doubt, the device's manual decides.
text.mbProfileAsk: Use profile {p}? Timeout {t} ms, pause after connecting {d} ms, pause between requests {g} ms. The port stays.
text.name: Name
text.ambiguous: Several identical adapters without a serial number: chosen by USB port (by-path). In Proxmox pass these through by port.
text.deviceSub: Suggested from the template and device; change it freely.
text.ifSerialSub: How the app talks to the device: {f}
text.ifNetSub: How programs connect to the device.
text.saveHintNew: Gets created, the others stay connected.
text.tuningSubMb: Pauses, cache, idle time, probe, units
text.netFollows: Who may connect: follows the setting {what}.
text.netLocalBind: Who may connect: this host only (bind address {a}).
text.bindWarn: The bind address {b} lets only this host in. Allowed clients elsewhere ({a}) cannot connect – clear the bind address or remove those clients.
text.maxClientsHint: More than 1 only if the device copes with it.
text.mode_raw: Bytes passed on unchanged – fits most integrations.
text.mode_rfc2217: Clients set baud rate and lines themselves (rfc2217://…).
text.o_hangup_when_done: Drop DTR when the last client leaves
text.o_low_latency: FTDI latency 1 ms instead of 16 ms
text.o_kickolduser: Disconnect an old client when full
text.o_chardelay: Collect bytes and send them together
text.sourcesub_device: A device connected by USB or serial.
text.sourcesub_tcp: A serial bridge in the network that takes only one client (ESPHome stream server, Tasmota reading head, USR-TCP232): the app connects to it and shares the data. Baud rate and format are set on the bridge.
text.o_meter_entities: Meter readings as entities (import, export, power over MQTT)
text.meterEntitiesHint: For the Energy dashboard: the app reads SML or D0 from what the meter sends anyway. The device must be open: a client connected or “Keep the device open”.
text.o_keep_open: Keep the device open (the app connects itself, takes a place)
text.o_stuck_disconnect: Disconnect the clients when one stops reading
text.o_notify_missing: Notify when the device is missing or does not answer
text.o_notify_no_client: Notify when no client is connected
text.remaddrHint: Empty: as the global setting. Addresses or networks, separated by spaces.
text.remaddrZwave: Preset is Home Assistant and apps only, because the stick takes commands and has no login.
text.silence: Warn when no data for (min, 0 = never)
text.silenceRestartHint: Only while the device is open (a client connected or “Keep the device open”). At most 3 times in a row, until data comes again.
text.discardConfirm: Discard your changes to this connection?
text.saveHint: Only this connection is rebuilt. The others stay connected.
text.effNone: No running connection is set up again, all clients stay connected.
text.deleteConfirm: Delete connection “{n}”? Its clients are disconnected.
text.importChoose: Where do the connections come from?
text.importFormats: ser2net 4 (YAML, version 1 and 2), ser2net 3 (ser2net.conf) or the options of ha-modbusproxy or modbus-proxy (YAML from its configuration tab)
text.importNone: I found no connections in it.
text.confl_port_device: Port {p} and the device are used by “{n}”
text.doneOff: Imported switched off: {n}. Check device paths and ports, then switch them on.
text.mergeSub: Existing ones stay; on a collision you choose per connection
text.doneText: The previous state is in the configuration history and can be restored there.
text.eventsSub: Everything since the app started, newest first.
text.eventsSubHistory: Kept for {d} days, with the stability of each connection.
text.startNowSub: After saving, the connection is reachable at once. Off: only saved, the port stays closed.
text.enabledSub: Off: the port is closed and connected clients are disconnected.
text.offConfirm: Switch off “{n}”? The {c} connected clients are disconnected.
text.importReplaceConfirm: {n} existing connections are replaced by the import. The old configuration stays in the config history and can be restored there.
text.moreEntries: … and {n} more entries – narrow them with the filters or the search
text.recNote: Disconnects no client; files rotate on their own.
text.liveCap: The last {n} lines in the browser, newest first – not the file.
text.noFiles: No files yet. They appear as soon as a connection records.
text.rotation: Rotation: {mb} MB per file · {k} older kept
text.netDeviateOne: One connection has its own bind address or allowed clients and does not follow this setting.
text.netDeviateMany: {n} connections have their own bind addresses or allowed clients and do not follow this setting.
text.sNetSub: Applies to all connections without their own bind address or their own allowed clients.
text.netsub_apps: e.g. Z-Wave JS UI, not from the LAN
text.netsub_lan_one: 1 network plus Home Assistant and apps
text.netsub_lan_many: {n} networks plus Home Assistant and apps
text.lanSub: Computers from these networks may connect. Home Assistant and apps are always allowed.
text.lanOwnUnknown: This host’s network is not known, so all private ranges apply.
text.lanErrFormat: That is not a valid network. Write it like 192.168.80.0/24
text.lanErrAll: That opens everything, the internet included. Choose “Anyone” instead.
text.lanErrDup: This network is already in the list.
text.lanNone: No network selected: only Home Assistant and apps may connect.
text.lanConfirm: Change the allowed networks? The clients of all connections are disconnected.
text.netWarn: ser2net has no login. Whoever reaches the port can read and control the device.
text.sBackupSub: One file with all connections and settings – for a new machine or as a backup.
text.backupMakeSub: Serial, Modbus and EnOcean. Contains the MQTT login – do not pass it on.
text.backupConfirm: Backup from {when}: {n} connections ({kinds}) and the settings. The {cur} current connections are replaced. The old state stays in the configuration history and can be restored there.
text.sSourceSub: Normally the app builds the ser2net file from your forms. For special cases you can use your own file instead.
text.srcFormsSub: Default · the app writes the file
text.srcOwnOn: Active · the forms no longer apply
text.srcOwnNone: None saved yet – create it below
text.ownCreateHint: Create your own file? It starts from the current forms.
text.fillConfirm: The text in the editor is replaced by the file built from the forms.
text.srcImportSub: Read a file, with a preview
text.srcExportSub: Serial connections only, for any ser2net 4
text.runtimeHint: This is how the app hands it to ser2net. It contains the app's admin interface. To take it along, use the export.
text.ownHint: Only serial connections are in this file. The app manages Modbus and EnOcean itself.
text.ownWarn: While your own file is in use, the forms are not used. No admin section: the app adds its own.
text.listenConfirm: Change who can reach the devices? The clients of all connections are disconnected.
text.ownConfirm: Use your own ser2net.yaml? All connections from the forms are switched off.
text.restoreConfirm: Restore this version? Changed connections are rebuilt.
text.brokenByChange: Since the change at {t}, what worked before does not: {n}.
text.logSub: How detailed the app logs and how long it keeps data.
text.logHint: Technical log for troubleshooting. You find it in Home Assistant under Settings → Apps → Device Proxy → Log. The connections' events are on the Events tab here in the panel instead. Applies at once.
text.historyDaysHint: Older entries on the Events tab are deleted.
text.debA: Sum up when the same event occurs
text.debHint: This keeps the log readable when, for example, a stick keeps dropping out.
text.trHint: Applies to connections with recording switched on.
text.traceCalc: At most about {mb} MB per connection ({size} MB × {files} files)
text.langHint: Applies to this browser only, and at once.
text.helpText: Have a problem? Download the diagnostics package and attach it to a bug report.
text.diagPrivacy: The names of your connections and device paths stay in. IP addresses, host names, logins and clients are removed. Take a quick look before you share it publicly.
text.toolOff: Not possible: the connection is switched off.
text.noData30Help: ser2net opens the device only while a client is connected – or with “keep device open”.
text.meterCheckSub: Reads the data of the last 30 s as SML or D0.
text.noData30: No data in the last 30 s.
text.baudDetectSub: Listens briefly at each baud rate and format; sends nothing. Takes up to about a minute; connected clients are disconnected and reconnect afterwards.
text.baudConfirm: For the detection ser2net lets go of the device for up to about a minute – this connection's clients are disconnected and connect again afterwards. Start?
text.sNotifySub: As a notification under Home Assistant's bell; optionally also to a phone.
text.notifyGraceHint: Short dropouts then raise no alarm.
text.noClientHint: Applies to connections with “Report when no client”.
text.noClientOff: No connection has “Report when no client” switched on.
text.nBell: Always in the Home Assistant bell.
text.notifyLanguageHint: Also applies to the names of the MQTT entities. The web interface has its own language under “Help and info”.
text.notifyDismiss: Remove the notification from the bell when the problem is gone
text.notifyResolved: Also tell the phone when it is OK again
text.notifyLanguage: Language of notifications and entity names
text.mqttWhatSerial: Serial: connected, clients, data rate, last data, line errors, switch
text.mqttWhatModbus: Modbus: reachable, requests, unanswered, answer time, switch
text.mqttWhatEvents: All: events that can start automations, e.g. device gone or new client
text.mqttAutoSub: Home Assistant provides it, e.g. Mosquitto.
text.mqttNoneFound: None found. Choose an own broker.
text.mqttPrefixHint: Must match the prefix of the MQTT integration in Home Assistant, usually homeassistant.
text.sMqttSub: Every connection shows up in Home Assistant as a device, with status, clients, data rate and a switch.
text.mqttOn: Create the connections as devices in Home Assistant
text.mqttNoteNone: Home Assistant names no MQTT broker, so the app creates no entities. If you use your own broker such as EMQX, enter it once.
text.mqttNoteLost: MQTT is not connected to {b}: {e}. The entities are not being updated.
text.mqttIdsHint: New entities begin with device_proxy_. Existing ones are changed here. Home Assistant does not adapt automations, scripts, dashboards and templates that use the old IDs.
text.mqttIdsNone: All entity IDs already begin with device_proxy_.
text.mqttIdsWarn: Used in automations, scripts, scenes or groups: {n}. They have to be adapted there. The preview does not check dashboards.
text.mqttIdsConfirm: Change {n} entity IDs? References to the old IDs are not adapted.
text.mqttNames: The names of the entities follow the language of the notifications.
text.kindsub_serial: USB or serial through ser2net, e.g. meters, Z-Wave stick
text.kindsub_modbus: Modbus TCP or RTU for several Modbus TCP clients, e.g. inverters
text.linksub_rtu_listen: A bus whose master asks already (e.g. inverter and meter): the app only listens, never sends and answers reads from what it heard. Writing is not possible.
text.mbListenAgeHint: Registers not heard for longer count as unknown: the client then gets exception 0B.
text.mbListenNone: Nothing heard yet. Does the master ask? Are baud rate and format right, A/B wired the right way?
text.mbListenDropped: {n} bytes fitted no frame (noise, wrong format)
text.linksub_tcp: A device in the network, e.g. inverter, heat pump, battery.
text.linksub_rtu: An RS485 adapter on this host – the app opens it itself.
text.linksub_rtu_tcp: An RS485-to-Ethernet converter in transparent mode.
text.mbClientsHint: Modbus TCP clients at the same time.
text.mbTimeoutHint: How long the proxy waits for the device.
text.mbRetriesHint: Repeats when the device does not answer.
text.mbConnectDelayHint: For devices that need a moment after the connection is made (connection_time).
text.mbPreviewSub: All requests go to the device one after another over one connection.
text.mbFlowQueueSub: one request after the other · timeout {ms} ms · {r}
text.liveSubMb: Requests to the device and its answers, with unit id and function.
text.liveEmptyMb: No requests yet. As soon as a client asks, requests and answers show here.
text.mbTipShare: Share of the time the device was taken up by the connected clients, since they connected
text.mbTipAnswer: How long the device takes on average for this client's requests
text.mbTipWait: How long this client's requests wait on average until the device is free
text.mbSharingOk: The clients do not slow each other down: longest average wait {w} ms.
text.mbSharingBusy: {n} waits {w} ms on average while the device answers in {a} ms: it is at capacity. Would the cache or a longer polling interval help?
text.mbTipFailed: Requests the device did not answer in time
text.mbTipExceptions: The device answered with a Modbus error reply (exception)
text.mbTipBlocked: Writes the write protection of this connection did not let through
text.mbWriteSub: Modbus has no login: otherwise whoever reaches the port can change registers on the device.
text.wasub_all: Read and write for every client, as with ha-modbusproxy.
text.wasub_listed: Read for all, write only for the addresses given.
text.wasub_none: Read only. Writes get exception 0x01 (illegal function).
text.mbWriteClientsHint: Addresses or networks. Home Assistant: 127.0.0.1, other apps: 172.30.32.0/23.
text.mbProbeSub: Reads one register when nobody asked for a while: “reachable” is then right without clients too, and the device does not close the connection for being idle.
text.mbProbeSeconds: After a quiet time of (s, 0 = off)
text.mbAddressHint: Address from 0, as in the frame (e.g. 40001 → 0).
text.mbWriteToolSub: Writes straight to the device. A wrong address or value can change its settings.
text.mbWriteLocked: Locked: writing is set to “Nobody” for this connection.
text.mbReadbackDiff: differs, the device did not take the value as written
text.mbDecodeSub: Reads the registers as Home Assistant's Modbus integration does: the same data type and “swap” give the same value there.
text.mbEntitiesSub: The app reads these registers itself and reports them to Home Assistant over MQTT, without any YAML. Easiest to add with Read registers → Decode values.
text.mbEntitiesHint: Unit function address type swap scale unit class name. No unit or class: -. A text of 8 registers: string:8. At most 50.
text.mbEntitySecondsHint: 5 to 3600. Each read goes to the device in turn with the clients.
text.mbEntityAddSub: With this type, swap and scale. The app then reads the register itself and reports it to Home Assistant over MQTT.
text.mbEntityAdded: Entity added. It appears in Home Assistant once MQTT is connected.
text.mbDecodeShort: Too few registers read: this data type needs {n}.
text.mbSensorYaml: Sensor for register {a} under the Modbus hub's sensors: in configuration.yaml:
text.mbWriteRulesHint: One line per client: address or network, then its registers, * for any or none for no register. The first line that fits applies instead of the registers above. Who may write at all is still decided by the choice above.
text.mbWriteRulesShort: {n} rule(s) of their own per client
text.acSub: What a client at this address may do, by the saved rules. Nothing is sent; a client on this host counts as 127.0.0.1.
text.ac_bind: No access: the port is open on {b} only, so only this host reaches it.
text.ac_own_rule: No access: this connection's allowed clients leave the address out.
text.ac_blocked: No access: this computer is blocked under Settings → Clients.
text.ac_network: No access: the network setting leaves the address out.
text.ac_write_access: May read but not write: the write access of {by} leaves the address out (exception 01).
text.ac_registers: May read but not write here: the register is outside the allowed registers of {by} (exception 02).
text.ac_listen_only: May read but not write: this connection only listens (exception 01).
text.ac_no_route: The unit goes to {r}, a connection that does not exist (exception 0A).
text.mbReadSub: Asks the device directly – in turn with the clients, without the cache.
text.mbScanSub: Finds the unit ids that answer (reads register 0), then asks them for vendor and model. With 247 units and 200 ms this takes up to about two minutes; the clients get their turns in between.
text.mbIdentifying: Asking the units found who they are …
text.mbUnitsSub: The clients' requests per device on the bus
text.mbUnitMapHint: client unit=device unit, e.g. 1=3, 2=5 – for clients that always ask unit 1. Empty: unchanged.
text.mbLinksHint: More than 1 only when the device allows that many at once; requests then run in parallel.
text.mbToolsSub: read and write registers, scan the bus
text.toolsSubSerial: detect the baud rate, check the meter
text.eoToolsSub: test the gateway, send a frame, record
text.haUiSteps: Usually the integration for your device is enough (e.g. SolarEdge Modbus): Settings → Devices & services → Add integration. As the connection choose the network connection (Modbus TCP) and enter host {h} and port {p}, to copy from the “Addresses” card.
text.haUnitHint: Enter the unit ID (called “device ID” in some integrations) as on the device, usually 1.
text.haYamlSummary: No integration for your device? Modbus in YAML
text.haYamlSub: Only needed when no integration supports your device: a Modbus hub in configuration.yaml.
text.haSnippetComment: sensors:, switches: … per entry address and device_address (= unit ID), see the docs
text.mbCacheHint: The same read from several clients within this time asks the device once. A write empties the cache.
text.connectionLost: No connection to the app – showing the last state.
text.usbEnoceanHint: This is an EnOcean gateway. As the kind “EnOcean gateway” the app checks its telegrams, shows its status and replays missed telegrams to Home Assistant.
text.kindsub_enocean: FAM-USB, FAM14, USB300, MGW … for several programs, with replay for Home Assistant
text.eoTemplateSub: Sets protocol, baud rate and kind of connection. Everything stays changeable.
text.fbSub: A second gateway with the same base ID takes over when this one fails. The programs stay on this port and notice nothing.
text.fbPick: When it fails, take over with
text.fbPickHint: EnOcean connections with the same protocol that are not a fallback already. Set the second gateway up as a normal connection first and check it there.
text.fbNoCandidates: There is no matching second gateway yet. Add it first as a normal EnOcean connection with the same protocol ({p}).
text.fbBaseDiffers: The base ID differs: {b} reports {theirs}, this gateway {mine}. {b} does not take over like this.
text.fbBaseUnknown: Base ID not known yet. The app compares them once both gateways are connected.
text.fbBusMain: A {t} sits on the RS485 bus of the series 14 and also brings the telegrams of the bus actuators. A fallback stands in for radio only: what comes over the bus alone is missing while it does.
text.fbBusFallback: {b} is a {t} on the RS485 bus. Two bus gateways with the same base ID on one bus get in each other's way; a radio gateway (FAM-USB, USB300, LAN) suits better as fallback.
text.fbIsFallback: This connection is the fallback of {a}. While it is, it has no port and no clients of its own; programs connect to {a}.
text.fbPortNote: Runs through {a}: port and clients rest while this connection is a fallback.
text.fbSwitchingSub: when the fallback takes over and when it hands back
text.fbtrigsub_probe: The app reads the base ID every {s} s. When the connection is gone or {n} reads stay unanswered, the fallback takes over.
text.fbProbeHint: 3 to 300. Checking more often notices a failure sooner.
text.fbMissesHint: 1 to 20. A silent gateway is replaced after about {t} s; too few reads switch over at a short dropout already.
text.fbStableHint: 5 to 3600, at least as long as "Check every". Shorter goes back sooner, but flips over more easily.
text.fbtrigsub_disconnect: The fallback takes over only when the connection to the gateway is gone.
text.fbretsub_auto: Once this gateway has run steadily for {s} s and nothing waits at the fallback.
text.fbretsub_manual: Stays on the fallback until you switch back on this gateway's page.
text.fbListenHint: The programs get the radio telegrams of both gateways; duplicates and the own sending are dropped. Gives more range.
text.fbConfirm: {b} becomes the fallback of {a}. Port {p} of {b} closes{clients}, and {b} is no longer offered to the integration. {base}
text.fbConfirmIntegration: The EnOcean Eltako integration is connected to {b}: remove the entry of {b} there afterwards, it stays disconnected otherwise. The devices belong to this gateway's entry.
text.fbConfirmIntegrationMaybe: If {b} is set up in the EnOcean Eltako integration, remove that entry afterwards; it stays disconnected otherwise.
text.fbDeleteNote: {n} is the fallback of {a}; {a} has none afterwards.
text.fbDeleteMain: {b} is this gateway's fallback and becomes a normal connection with its own port again.
text.fbReturnAuto: Back: automatically after {s} s of steady running
text.fbManualNote: Switched by hand: stays on the fallback until you switch back.
text.fbSwitchConfirm: Switch to {b}? The programs of {a} then send and receive through {b} until you switch back.
text.fbPromoteSub: When this gateway is broken: {a} takes over the hardware of {b} and keeps its name, port, clients and history. The old hardware goes to the connection {b}.
text.fbPromoteConfirm: {a} uses {new} from now on. The old hardware ({old}): {what}. Both connections restart; the replay bridges the short gap.
text.fbReason_base_id_unknown: the fallback's base ID is not known yet
text.fbReason_own_base_id_unknown: the own base ID is not known yet
text.eoIt_fallback: The own gateway failed ({r}); {b} stands in since {t}. The programs stay connected.
text.eoIt_fallbackHand: Switched by hand; {b} sends and receives for the programs since {t}, until you switch back.
text.eoIt_fbUnready: {r}. If this gateway fails, nothing takes over.
text.eoIt_serves: No port, no clients of its own. Ready in case {a} fails.
text.eoIt_servesActive: No port, no clients of its own. Standing in for {a} right now.
text.eoModelHint: Goes to the EnOcean integration with the discovery. The app cannot tell by itself, it only passes bytes on.
text.eoHostHint: Address of the gateway or of a ser2net on the network.
text.eoPortHint: The EnOcean integration gets it through discovery. Usually from 9100.
text.eoClientsHint: Home Assistant, eo_man, PCT14 … at the same time.
text.eoGapHint: After each frame to the gateway, so it does not overflow.
text.eoReplaySub: Radio telegrams that arrive while Home Assistant restarts are delivered afterwards.
text.eoPersistHint: Survives a restart of this app too.
text.eoAccessSub: Replace old clients, idle timeout, trace
text.eoAllowedHint: Empty: as the global setting, so eo_man or PCT14 in the home network can connect at once. For less, give addresses or networks separated by spaces, or use the button below.
text.eoFlowQueueSub: {ms} ms pause · answers only to the one who asked
text.eoHaOnlyNote: Only Home Assistant and other apps can connect, computers in the LAN cannot. "Follow the global setting" brings back the network setting.
text.eoBaseSub: Sets the gateway's base ID. It is kept in flash and can be changed only a few times (10 times for TCM 300 modules) – after that it stays for good. Taught-in actuators know the old ID and must be taught in again.
text.eoBaseRange: FF-80-00-00 to FF-FF-FF-80, last byte 00 or 80
text.eoBaseSame: This is already the current base ID
text.eoBaseConfirm: Change the base ID of {n} to {id}? Taught-in actuators must be taught in again afterwards.
text.eoBaseConfirmUnknown: This gateway does not report how many changes are left.
text.eoBaseR_not_supported: The gateway cannot change its base ID
text.eoBaseR_flash_error: The gateway could not write its flash
text.eoBaseR_out_of_range: The gateway does not take this base ID
text.eoBaseR_no_writes_left: No changes left – the base ID stays as it is
text.eoBaseR_no_answer: No answer from the gateway – the base ID above shows what applies
text.eoAirSub: Sending time of the last hour
text.eoAirHigh: Close to the limit. Home Assistant was notified
text.eoRbSub: Radio telegrams for programs after a restart
text.eoRbCollect: Collecting until a program is connected
text.eoRbLive: A program with replay is connected
text.eoRbFullWarn: Full: the oldest telegrams are dropped
text.eoRbDisk: Survives a restart of the app
text.eoIt_port: Another program holds the port: {e}. Choose another port.
text.eoIt_missing: {d} is missing. Check the USB cable and the device path.
text.eoIt_down: {e}. The app keeps trying; programs stay connected, their frames are dropped.
text.eoIt_duty: Of the allowed 1 % per hour. Beyond it the gateway delays or drops telegrams. Send less or check automations.
text.eoIt_locked: A recording runs; only {peer} may send. Frames of the other programs (Home Assistant too) are dropped and not sent later.
text.eoIt_queue: The programs send faster than the gateway takes them.
text.eoIt_dropped: Sent while the gateway was disconnected.
text.eoIt_slow: It stopped reading; otherwise its data would grow without bound.
text.eoIt_refused: Its address is not listed under "Allowed clients".
text.eoIt_held: During a recording with a lock; they were not sent later.
text.eoIt_noClients: Programs connect on port {port}. The EnOcean integration finds the gateway itself.
text.liveSubEo: Every frame with kind and sender – click an ID to show only that sender.
text.eoReserved: Reserved for {peer} while the recording runs.
text.eoTestSub: Reads the base ID ten times: how fast and reliably the gateway answers. Sends nothing over the air.
text.eoTestResult: {a} of {s} answered · avg {avg} ms · max {max} ms
text.eoSendSub: One whole {p} frame as hex. Checked while you type.
text.eoBadHex: Hex digit pairs only (spaces, : and - allowed).
text.eoHcrc: Header CRC wrong, it should be {want}.
text.eoLen3: The header says {want} bytes, this has {n}.
text.eoDcrc: Data CRC wrong, it should be {want}.
text.eoCaptureSub: A single recording of every frame (JSON lines, at most 50 MB). The file then appears under "Trace". Unlike the permanent trace it can reserve sending for one program.
text.eoLockHint: For PCT14 with a FAM14: let only this program send, so nobody interferes.
text.eoCaptureOther: A recording of {n} is running already.
text.eoPct14Steps: Connect PCT14 on the PC to this port (through a ser2net/network adapter)|Choose the PC here as the only program that may send|Start the recording, read or write in PCT14|Stop the recording and download the file under "Trace"
text.sEnoceanSub: For the EnOcean Eltako integration in Home Assistant.
text.eoNoGateway: These settings take effect once you add an EnOcean connection.
text.eoDiscovery: Offer the gateways to the EnOcean Eltako integration
text.eoDiscoveryHint: The integration then finds the gateways itself and sets them up, including replay (delivering missed radio telegrams).
text.eoStatusPortHint: The integration reads the connection, air time and replay here. Only for Home Assistant and other apps, refused from the LAN. Also runs when the gateways are not offered. Default 9199, change it only if the port is taken.
text.eoStatusClosed: Status port {port} is not open ({e}). The app tries again every 30 s; until then the integration shows "proxy status not reachable". If another program has the port, choose a different one under "Advanced".

events.auto_restart_gave_up: Still no data after {count} automatic restarts: no further restarts until data comes
events.exclusive_off: Maintenance over ({reason}): all allowed clients may connect again
events.enocean_failover: Running on the fallback {fallback} ({reason}), {unanswered} commands unanswered
events.enocean_failback: Back on its own gateway, the fallback {fallback} rests ({reason})
events.enocean_fallback_promoted: The fallback's hardware taken over: now {new}; old hardware ({old}): {action}
events.custom_invalid: Own ser2net.yaml cannot be used, nothing is shared: {errors}

notes.device_missing_unstable: Device {device} is not plugged in right now and may change after a restart – better choose a by-id or by-path name.
notes.device_missing: Device {device} is not plugged in right now.
notes.device_unstable: {device} may change after a restart – better choose a by-id or by-path name.
notes.option_extra: Option {option} kept as a further option.
notes.remaddr_port_dropped: remaddr {address}: the client port is dropped.
notes.trace_files_moved: Trace files are replaced by the app's trace.
notes.option_unsafe: Option {option} not taken over: it is not allowed here (starts programs, reads files or needs a login).
notes.accepter_unsupported: Accepter {accepter} is not supported (TCP, telnet, RFC2217 only).
notes.connector_unsupported: Connector {connector} is not supported (serial devices only).
notes.admin_ignored: Admin section ignored – the app has its own.
notes.admin_present: The file has an admin section – please remove it, the app adds its own.
notes.port_reserved: Port {port} is reserved for the app.
notes.port_modbus: Port {port} ({name}) is held by the app's connection "{modbus}" already.
notes.legacy_format: ser2net 4 cannot read the old format (ser2net.conf) – please import it.
notes.modbus_stop_old: Stop ha-modbusproxy before taking over – both cannot listen on the same port.

new_clients: {count} computers connected for the first time. Mark them as known, name or block them under Settings → Clients.
new_client: {address} connected to {name} on {since}, for the first time. Known? Then mark it as known under Settings → Clients or give it a name.
silence: No data from the device since {since}.
stuck: Device Proxy: {name} – client does not read
{address} stopped reading; all clients of this connection are slowed down.
line_errors: Line errors are rising ({count} since start) – check baud rate and format.
ser2net: ser2net ended {count}× in the last 10 minutes. See the app log.
duty: Device Proxy: {name} – air time nearly used up
{share} % of the allowed air time (1 %) was used in the last hour. Beyond it the gateway delays or drops telegrams.
fallback: Device Proxy: {name} – running on the fallback
{fallback} stands in since {since} ({reason}). The programs notice nothing.
fallback_unready: {fallback} could not stand in if the gateway failed: {reason}.
custom: Your own ser2net.yaml is not used, nothing is shared. See the app's settings.

reasons.base_id_unknown: the fallback's base ID is not known yet
reasons.own_base_id_unknown: the own base ID is not known yet
